purpose: Fix 6 performance/quality issues in JS frontend: replace setInterval+async with recursive setTimeout to prevent overlapping poll executions, migrate from Math.random() to useId(), cache DOM queries in focus trap, conditionally activate safety scan, and properly await suggestion fetching.
riskRationale: All changes are isolated to JS frontend files using well-understood patterns (recursive setTimeout, React useId, ref caching). No PHP, security, or data-layer changes. One bounded concurrency concern exists but has a straightforward fix.

text: Well-structured PR that correctly addresses real race conditions in async polling loops. The recursive setTimeout pattern in Dashboard.js and PageSpeedPanel.js prevents overlapping API calls that could occur with setInterval+async. The useId() migration, cached DOM queries, and conditional safety scan are solid quality improvements. One important issue found: in Dashboard.js, the recursive setTimeout can be overwritten by optimizeImages, creating a window for concurrent poll schedules to compound. Fix is straightforward. Two minor issues also noted for ConfirmDialog cleanup and lazyload activation guard.

reasoning: One important fix needed in Dashboard.js (pollingRef.current race window) where optimizeImages can fire mid-pollJobStatus, leading to concurrent poll schedules that compound. Fix is 3 lines and well-understood. Two minor improvements also recommended. All other changes are correct and merge-worthy.

message: Correct recursive setTimeout pattern in pollJobStatus. Properly serializes async execution by calling setTimeout only after the previous poll resolves, preventing overlapping API calls that could occur with setInterval + async callbacks. The guard at line 209 correctly prevents rescheduling when pollingRef.current has been externally nullified.

Consistent recursive setTimeout fix applied in pollForResults. The self-scheduling approach ensures each poll tick waits for the previous getPagespeedResults() call to complete before scheduling the next, preventing concurrent scan status requests.

Clean migration from Math.random() to React 18's useId(). Provides collision-free, SSR-safe IDs and eliminates the useRef wrapper. The id value correctly connects aria-describedby to the tooltip span's id attribute.
Caching querySelectorAll results in focusableRef via useEffect avoids redundant DOM queries on every Tab keydown — a solid accessibility micro-optimization.

Well-factored extraction of startSafetyScan into a named helper with early-return guard. Conditional activation (only when MutationObserver detects lazy elements or initial elements exist) avoids running an unnecessary 10s interval when the DOM has no lazy content.

Moving fetchSuggestions from a fire-and-forget .then().catch() to an explicit await with inner try/catch eliminates unhandled promise rejection risk. The sequential dependency between scan completion and suggestions fetching is now explicit, and scan UI state changes remain cleanly separated from the suggestions fetch.

Race window: when optimizeImages fires during an in-flight pollJobStatus (setting pollingRef.current to a new setTimeout), the completing pollJobStatus overwrites pollingRef.current when rescheduling, losing the reference to optimizeImages's timeout. Both timeouts remain active, leading to concurrent pollJobStatus invocations that each reschedule themselves, compounding over cycles.
suggestion: Capture pollingRef.current at the start of pollJobStatus and only reschedule if it hasn't been externally changed. This ensures external callers (like optimizeImages) who set a fresh timeout take precedence over the stale scheduled tick from the completing poll execution.

message: focusableRef.current is not cleared when the dialog closes (isOpen→false), retaining stale DOM element references until the dialog reopens.
suggestion: Reset focusableRef.current to an empty array in the effect cleanup when isOpen becomes false, so unmounted DOM nodes are released for garbage collection.

message: startSafetyScan() is called unconditionally for every MutationObserver callback where nodeType===1, even if the added node contains no lazy-loadable elements.
suggestion: Guard the startSafetyScan() call behind a check for whether the node subtree actually contains lazy elements, e.g. `if (node.matches(LAZY_SELECTOR) || node.querySelector(LAZY_SELECTOR)) startSafetyScan()`. This avoids unnecessary function calls on non-lazy DOM mutations.
